author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be reopened by its own address and its date and description corrected in place; the same visit record is updated rather than a new one added, and correction reuses booking's validation. Cancelling stays out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Reopening a booked visit for correction shows the visit form prefilled with the visit's current date and description.
Submitting a valid description and a date later than today updates that same visit's date and description in place, adds no further visit to the pet, and then shows the owner's record.
Submitting a blank description, or a date of today or earlier, refuses the correction, names the offending field, and leaves the visit unchanged.
Correction is reachable only by its own address; no link to it is added to the owner's record in this slice.
non_goals: Cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5, NG-4)
Adding a link to visit correction from the owner's record
notes: Narrows NG-5 per adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md. GET and POST share one address ending in /edit; POST validates identically to visit creation. Open question recorded in PRD: whether to surface a correction link on the owner's record (deferred follow-up). ADR index in docs/adr/README.md still needs the new row added by its owner.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the existing owner feature package unchanged. Visit correction is the create-or-update controller pattern already demonstrated by PetController (Read of PetController.java: initUpdateForm/processUpdateForm at lines 139-179 and the in-place updatePetDetails at 186-200 that mutates the existing entity via setX then owners.saveAndFlush) applied to VisitController, plus aggregate-navigation-by-identity already demonstrated by Owner.getPet(Integer) (Read of Owner.java:117-127). No new module, no service layer, no new repository — writes stay on OwnerRepository per the aggregate write-path rule in system-design.md Contracts. The one small structural addition is a Pet.getVisit(Integer id) accessor mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id). IDE oracle not connected this run; resolution claims are Read-based (weaker basis than search_symbol).
integration_points: Add GET+POST @RequestMapping for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit on VisitController, sharing the single /edit address for both verbs (form posts to current URL, no th:action needed).

The @ModelAttribute("visit") loadPetWithVisit method must branch on an optional @PathVariable(name="visitId", required=false) Integer visitId: for /new keep returning a fresh Visit added via pet.addVisit(visit); for /edit return the EXISTING visit located by pet.getVisit(visitId) and do NOT call pet.addVisit. Mirror PetController.findPet's required=false optional-id branch.
Add Pet.getVisit(Integer id) that scans pet.getVisits() and returns the matching visit or null, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id).

In-place update: the edit @ModelAttribute returns the existing visit, Spring binds the submitted date/description onto that same instance (id stays disallowed), then owners.save(owner) persists via cascade — the same row is updated, no visit added. Alternatively copy fields onto the existing visit as updatePetDetails does; either satisfies the same-record requirement so long as no pet.addVisit runs on the edit path.
Redirect target on success is redirect:/owners/{ownerId}, identical to booking (owner record / AC-2).

patterns.description: create-or-update controller: shared template, /edit GET returns the form, POST validates and updates in place, redirect to owner
in-place update via existing-entity setX + owners.saveAndFlush — the model for updating the same record rather than adding one
aggregate navigation by identity (getPet(Integer)); Pet.getVisit(Integer) should mirror it
the non-future-date rejection (typeMismatch.visitDate) to reuse verbatim on the edit POST alongside @Valid @NotBlank description

risks.risk: The current loadPetWithVisit unconditionally calls pet.addVisit(visit); reusing it as-is for the edit path would add a second visit, violating AC-2 (adds no further visit).
risks.mitigation: Branch on visitId presence: only add for the /new path; the /edit path returns the existing visit and never calls addVisit.

risks.risk: A visitId that belongs to another pet or does not exist could NPE or, worse, edit a foreign visit (IDOR-shaped).
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only through pet.getVisit(visitId) (pet-scoped, no global visit lookup exists); a null result must fail cleanly with IllegalArgumentException like the existing missing-pet guard in loadPetWithVisit. Pet-scoped navigation inherently confines correction to a visit owned by the pet in the path — a security-by-design property, now recorded in system-design.md Contracts invariants.

risks.risk: On validation failure the in-memory existing visit has been mutated by binding.
risks.mitigation: The error path must return the view WITHOUT calling owners.save, leaving the persisted visit unchanged (AC-3). No flush on the error path.

risks.risk: Duplicated non-future-date + description validation across the new and edit POST handlers.
risks.mitigation: Optional DRY extraction into a private helper; duplication is consistent with the codebase (PetController duplicates the birthDate check across create/update), so leaving it inline is acceptable and this is an inner-loop Refactor call, not a design blocker.

notes: Verdict minor: existing PetController create-or-update pattern + Owner aggregate navigation cover the design; the small adjustments are Pet.getVisit(Integer), the optional-visitId branch on the visit model attribute, and the edit routes. No new ADR — the product decision is already recorded in adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md (owned by product-requirements-expert), and the how (reuse the in-repo create-or-update mirror) is not a hard-to-reverse trade-off. Durable-memory writes this dispatch: docs/adr/README.md gained the 2026-08-27 index row; docs/system-design.md Contracts rows for VisitController/Visit/Owner/Pet/OwnerRepository gained REQ-VISITEDIT-001 and the aggregate-navigation invariant now records visit-through-pet-by-identity. Template guidance: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html likely needs no structural change — it has no th:action (posts to the current /edit URL), th:object=${visit} prefills date/description from the existing visit (AC-1), and ${visit['new']} is false for an existing visit so the heading drops "New" and the Previous Visits table renders; the only optional nicety is a context-aware submit label (addVisit vs an edit label), which no acceptance criterion requires. Guardrails: keep setDisallowedFields("id","*.id") (mass-assignment guard); add no link to the edit page from the owner detail template (AC-4 / NG scope). Next specialist: feature-implementer (TDD) against the five test_names in the prd-entry.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: IDOR confined: the edit visit is resolved only through the pet-scoped chain owners.findById(ownerId) -> owner.getPet(petId) -> pet.getVisit(visitId); each miss throws IllegalArgumentException, and no global visit lookup exists, so a visitId belonging to another pet or owner cannot be reached or mutated
Mass-assignment guard retained: setDisallowedFields("id","*.id") blocks rebinding the visit/nested identity, so binding cannot redirect the persisted record
In-place update binds onto the pet-scoped existing Visit instance returned by @ModelAttribute("visit"); owners.save cascades on the owner aggregate, no foreign entity touched

No injection or path-traversal surface: visitId is a typed Integer path variable used only for an in-memory scan; exception messages concatenate numeric ids only; description/date render through the unchanged auto-escaping Thymeleaf template
Validation-failure path returns the view without owners.save, leaving the persisted visit unchanged

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All five new test methods use the `should{Outcome}` prefix instead of the brief-required `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` school (testing-principles.md § Test Naming, effective 2026-07-31). Examples: `shouldShowVisitFormPrefilledWhenCorrectingAnExistingVisit` → `theVisitFormShouldBePrefillledWithCurrentDataWhenCorrectingAnExistingVisit`; `shouldUpdateExistingVisitInPlaceWhenCorrectionIsValid` → `theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlaceWhenValid`; `shouldRedirectToOwnerRecordAfterSuccessfulCorrection` → `theVisitCorrectionShouldRedirectToOwnerRecordAfterSuccess`; `shouldRejectCorrectionWithBlankDescription` → `theVisitCorrectionShouldRejectABlankDescription`; `shouldRejectCorrectionWithDateNotInTheFuture` → `theVisitCorrectionShouldRejectADateThatIsNotInTheFuture`. The prd-entry `test_names` list also recorded the `should` form, which produced a prd/brief disagreement followed downstream — both the prd-entry and the implementation need the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` form.
findings.fix: Rename all five methods to the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` pattern. Update the prd-entry `test_names` field to match so the handoff ledger agrees with the brief.

findings.description: The `@BeforeEach` setUp constructs `new Owner()`, `new Pet()`, and `new Visit()` directly. Testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction requires factory methods for all tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward, and this `@BeforeEach` was modified (adding the visit fixture) as part of this slice. Three factory calls are needed: `createAnOwner()`, `createAPet()`, and a `createAVisitWithIdDateAndDescription(TEST_VISIT_ID, ORIGINAL_VISIT_DATE, ORIGINAL_VISIT_DESCRIPTION)` (or equivalent anonymous factory with named overrides). The existing pre-2026-07-31 construction in the class is pre-existing debt, but the additions in this slice require factory wrapping from the start.
findings.fix: Introduce `createAnOwner()`, `createAPet()`, and `createAVisit(int id, LocalDate date, String description)` static factory methods in the test class. Replace the direct constructor calls added in this slice's `@BeforeEach` with the factories.

findings.description: The string literal `"Corrected checkup"` appears twice in `shouldUpdateExistingVisitInPlaceWhenCorrectionIsValid` — once as a POST param and once as an assertion expected value — without being named as a constant. Testing-principles.md § Three-Tier Data Naming Convention requires Tier-1 meaningful values to be named by role; `"Corrected checkup"` drives the outcome being asserted and qualifies as a meaningful value. `ORIGINAL_VISIT_DESCRIPTION` at line 63 sets the right precedent for this class.
findings.fix: Extract `private static final String CORRECTED_VISIT_DESCRIPTION = "Corrected checkup";` at the class level and use it in both `.param("description", CORRECTED_VISIT_DESCRIPTION)` and the assertion.

recommendations: The verify(never()).save() assertion couples the rejection tests to the persistence method name rather than to the observable outcome (visit unchanged). A future slice could replace this with a real in-memory repository double (no Mockito) and assert the stored state directly — the brief's preferred direction (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy). Not a blocker in this slice because OwnerRepository is already mocked class-wide and the prd-entry specified this approach.

The date constant LocalDate.now().plusDays(3) used in shouldUpdateExistingVisitInPlaceWhenCorrectionIsValid as both the POST param and the assertion expected value is correct (derived, not a magic number) but could be extracted to a local CORRECTED_VISIT_DATE variable for symmetry with ORIGINAL_VISIT_DATE.
approved_aspects: All five REQ-VISITEDIT-001 acceptance criteria have dedicated, passing tests: GET prefill (AC-1), in-place update with no extra visit and same visit ID (AC-2), owner-record redirect (AC-2), blank-description rejection (AC-3), past-date rejection (AC-3)

shouldUpdateExistingVisitInPlaceWhenCorrectionIsValid correctly asserts hasSize(1) on pet.getVisits(), getId().isEqualTo(TEST_VISIT_ID), and the updated fields — directly verifying the aggregate root carries the corrected state rather than a new record
ORIGINAL_VISIT_DATE and ORIGINAL_VISIT_DESCRIPTION named constants follow the Tier-1 convention for the prefill assertion
Rejection tests assert the correct error field, error code (typeMismatch.visitDate), HTTP 200, and correct view name — matching the booking path's validation pattern

verify(never()).save() on OwnerRepository is within the brief's tolerated boundary: OwnerRepository is a system boundary mock already present in the class, and the prd-entry explicitly specified this assertion shape for both rejection tests
Tests are all green (BUILD SUCCESSFUL)

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit's date and description

blast_radius.note: Two prod files in the single owner module (Pet.getVisit lookup, VisitController edit handlers) plus its test class and docs/ADR; no sensitive paths, and the 27 hunks are mostly documentation and tests.

semantic_surprise.note: The edit path mirrors booking: loadPetWithVisit resolves the existing visit pet-scoped by visitId (throwing if not owned by the pet), returns it as the bound model attribute so form binding mutates it in place, id stays disallowed from binding, and the same non-future-date rejection applies; nothing behaves beyond what the diff and description imply.

test_adequacy.note: Tests assert real outcomes rather than restating code: GET prefills current date/description, valid POST leaves the pet with one visit of the same id but updated fields, and blank-description and non-future-date cases reject with field errors and verify owners.save is never called.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four rosters end at approved with empty findings; the first-round changes_requested from code-quality, test, and doc were resolved in the second round and security approved outright, leaving no lingering caveats or escalations.

scope_deviation.note: One design revision, zero build retries and zero consultations; the change stays inside the NG-5 narrowing (correction in, cancellation out), and prd/system-design/ADR were updated to match the exact surface implemented.

rationale: All five facets read clear against the diff: a contained, well-tested edit-visit feature whose correction path faithfully mirrors booking, resolves visits pet-scoped to prevent cross-pet tampering, and updates in place. Confirm and merge; a quick read of VisitController.loadPetWithVisit suffices.
